Subject: Post-call: LuminaHealth - p95 SLA & procurement path

Hi Amy — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our side and a small set of follow-ups so we can route the right materials internally at Lumina.

Recap (from our notes)
- Primary use case: on-demand clinical note summarization and anonymized extraction during triage (PHI in scope).
- Scale: ~30k calls/day initially, burst to 100k/day monthly; average input length ~600 tokens, peak 2k tokens.
- Key decision criteria you called out: p95 inference latency, deployment mode (hosted vs private/VPC/on-prem), and procurement path for PHI-enabled workloads.

Questions we promised to confirm:
1) p95 target: can you confirm the numeric target you want us to architect for? (you mentioned ~200ms during the call; want to confirm whether that's a hard requirement or a goal)
2) Economic buyer & procurement owner: please confirm who will sign the PO (CTO vs procurement) and the procurement contact email.
3) Security gating: is SOC 2 Type II a minimum? Any additional requirements (DLP, SIEM integration, data residency)?

What we will send by EOD:
- Lightweight SOC2 summary + audit scope (attachment)
- Two cost/hosting options (hosted API + reserved Dedicated pool) with p95/throughput tradeoffs and a ballpark number for committed annual capacity
- Link to our standard procurement checklist and next steps for VPC/private onboarding

Proposed next step: 30-min sync with your procurement owner and Michael Park (CTO) so we can align the SOW + commercial terms. How does Mon May 3 10:00-10:30 PT look?

Thanks — I looped in Ben (pricing leads) and Neha (security/solutions) to keep this compact.

—Marissa

Subject: Re: Post-call: LuminaHealth - p95 SLA & procurement path

Thanks Marissa — good notes and appreciate the clarity. A few quick answers from our side.

1) p95: target is 180ms for inference for our typical payload (~600 tokens). That is our target SLA for the production integration; we can accept a phased approach (e.g., 200–220ms during pilot but 180ms for full roll-out).
2) Economic buyer: Michael Park (CTO) will sign high-level commercial terms; procurement handle is procurement@luminahealth.com (Emily Carter, Sr. Procurement Manager). I will introduce Emily on the procurement thread if we need standard RFP/procurement forms.
3) Security: SOC 2 Type II is required. We also need either a VPC/private deployment or a hosted tenant with dedicated encryption keys (KMS) and audited access controls. SIEM integration is required (they use Splunk) — we can share specific endpoints.

Can you give ballpark ARR and committed capacity thresholds tied to the p95 commitments? If you can send the two hosting options and a rough price band now, we can decide whether to involve IT/Security right away.

Yes — Mon May 3 10:00 PT works for a short alignment call with Michael and Emily.

Best,
Amy Jensen
Director, Platform Integrations
amy.jensen@luminahealth.com
LuminaHealth

Amy — looping in a quick options sketch so you have something concrete ahead of Mon's alignment call. Attached: "2027-04-28-lumina-estimate.xlsx" and our SOC2 summary (SOC2_summary.pdf).

High-level hosting options (ballpark, need final sizing to confirm):

Option A — Hosted API (Redwood multi-tenant with dedicated keys)
- Expected p95: ~150–200ms (600-token median), depends on model family and batching behavior.
- Pricing band: $120k–$220k ARR for initial volume (30k calls/day, bursts) depending on committed tokens and model choice.
- Pros: fastest to onboard, no infra work on Lumina side; Cons: you rely on Redwood-managed infra (we provide KMS integration + SIEM hooks).

Option B — Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in our cloud)
- Expected p95: ~120–160ms with reserved capacity tuned to your peak bursts.
- Pricing band: $210k–$380k ARR (includes reserved capacity and support SLA).
- Pros: predictable latency and SLOs, stronger isolation; Cons: requires commitment (12-month typical).

Option C — Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Expected p95: ~100–150ms but highly dependent on your local infra and networking; requires separate SOW.
- Pricing: custom; requires procurement lead time for infra & network setup.

Security checklist & gating items we recommend for PHI:
- SOC2 Type II report (attached summary)
- KMS/HSM integration for key separation
- SIEM forwarding to Splunk (we have a standard connector)
- Data retention and deletion policy doc

Proposed next steps
1) Share the attached estimate with procurement@luminahealth.com (Emily).
2) Quick technical sync between Neha and your security/IT to scope SIEM/KMS end points (30–45 min).
3) Commercial call with Michael + Emily + Marissa to finalize which option and term length (Mon May 3, 10:00 PT).

If you want a tighter p95 commitment (e.g., 180ms contractual), we can map an SLA with credits and require reserved capacity / Dedicated tier. Happy to walk through the tradeoffs on Monday.

—Ben
